cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Passwords should be stored only as the output of a slow, salted password-hashing function: Argon2id (preferred), bcrypt or scrypt. Never plain text and never encrypted, so a stolen database cannot be turned back into passwords quickly.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Each user gets a unique random salt so identical passwords produce different hashes and rainbow tables fail. The cost factor makes every guess expensive. The stored string holds algorithm, cost, salt and hash. At login the entered password is hashed with the same salt and cost and compared in constant time.

questions.q: Why not use SHA-256 plus a salt?
questions.a: SHA-256 is built to be fast; a GPU computes billions per second, so leaked salted hashes can still be cracked quickly.

questions.q: What does a per-user salt prevent?
questions.a: Identical passwords producing identical hashes, and the use of precomputed rainbow tables.

questions.q: What is stored in the hash string?
questions.a: The algorithm, the cost factor, the salt and the hash.
